subject: anaesthesia
title: Difficult Airway Management: Algorithms, Supraglottic Devices, and Front-of-Neck Access

steps.title: LEMON Airway Assessment
steps.tx: **LEMON difficult airway assessment** provides a systematic clinical framework: Look externally for facial trauma, micrognathia, or beard; Evaluate the 3-3-2 rule (three fingerbreadth mouth opening, three fingerbreadth hyomental distance, two fingerbreadth thyrohyoid distance); assess Mallampati score; evaluate airway Obstruction (epiglottitis, peritonsillar abscess, stridor); and test Neck mobility (atlanto-occipital extension greater than 35 degrees).

steps.title: Supraglottic Airway Devices
steps.tx: **Supraglottic airway device evolution** spans first-generation and second-generation designs: the classic Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA) features an inflatable silicone mask seating over the hypopharynx to seal the laryngeal inlet. Second-generation devices incorporate a dedicated gastric drain channel to vent stomach liquids and reduce aspiration risk; the ProSeal LMA achieves high seal pressures of 30 cmH2O, while the i-gel utilizes a preformed non-inflatable thermoplastic elastomer cuff.

steps.title: Awake Flexible Bronchoscopic Intubation
steps.tx: **Awake flexible fibreoptic intubation** remains the undisputed gold standard for anticipated difficult airways, severe maxillofacial deformities, morbid obesity, or unstable cervical spine fractures. The airway is meticulously prepared using topical local anaesthetics (nebulized 4 percent lignocaine and transtracheal recurrent laryngeal nerve blocks) and antisialagogue glycopyrrolate, allowing intubation over the bronchoscope while the patient maintains spontaneous respiration and airway reflexes.

steps.title: Video Laryngoscopy Principles
steps.tx: **Video laryngoscopy optical advantages** overcome limited direct line-of-sight visual axes by positioning a high-definition digital camera chip and light-emitting diode at the distal tip of the blade. Hyperangulated blades (such as the GlideScope) visualize the anterior glottis without requiring sniffing position alignment, demanding a rigid pre-shaped stylet to guide the endotracheal tube around the steep curvature into the trachea.

left.title: Standard Direct Laryngoscopy
points: Requires physical alignment of oral, pharyngeal, and laryngeal axes
Fails when cervical spine mobility or mouth opening is limited
Direct line-of-sight illumination from mouth entrance

right.title: Hyperangulated Video Laryngoscopy
points: Digital micro-camera looks around anatomical corner directly
Provides panoramic view of vocal cords without neck extension
Requires dedicated curved rigid stylet for tube delivery

steps.title: Gum Elastic Bougie Tactile Signs
steps.tx: **Gum elastic bougie intubation tactile signs** distinguish tracheal entry from accidental esophageal passage when direct glottic exposure is restricted to a Cormack-Lehane Grade III view. Advancing the angled 40-degree coudé tip down the trachea produces distinct palpable clicks as the tip rubs against anterior cartilaginous tracheal rings, followed by a firm hold-up resistance at 24 to 40 centimeters upon reaching the carina.

steps.title: Can't Intubate Can't Oxygenate (CICO)
steps.tx: **Can not intubate can not oxygenate emergency** represents the ultimate airway crisis, declared when tracheal intubation fails, bag-mask ventilation is impossible, and rescue supraglottic airway insertion fails to maintain arterial oxygenation. Cognitive aids mandate calling for emergency multidisciplinary assistance, declaring CICO aloud to the operating theatre team, awakening the patient if feasible, and proceeding instantly to emergency front-of-neck access.

steps.title: Scalpel-Bougie-Tube Cricothyroidotomy
steps.tx: **Scalpel bougie tube cricothyroidotomy** is the definitive, fastest technique for emergency front-of-neck access endorsed by the Difficult Airway Society. The clinician identifies the cricothyroid membrane, executes a transverse stab incision through the skin and membrane with a size 10 scalpel blade, turns the blade 90 degrees to hold the stoma open, slides a coudé-tipped bougie into the trachea, and railroads a cuffed 6.0 mm endotracheal tube into place.

steps.title: Double-Lumen Tubes for Lung Isolation
steps.tx: **Double-lumen endobronchial tube mechanics** provide independent one-lung ventilation during thoracic surgery. Left-sided double-lumen tubes are preferred universally because the right mainstem bronchus gives off the right upper lobe bronchus merely 1.5 to 2 centimeters from the carina, making right-sided tubes highly prone to right upper lobe bronchial cuff obstruction. Positioning must be confirmed immediately via flexible fiberoptic bronchoscopy.

left.title: Left-Sided Double-Lumen Tube
points: Long left mainstem bronchus (4 to 5 cm) provides safe bronchial cuff seating
Universal standard tube for almost all thoracic procedures
Low risk of lobar bronchial orifice occlusion

right.title: Right-Sided Double-Lumen Tube
points: Short right mainstem bronchus (1.5 to 2 cm) before upper lobe takeoff
Requires special slotted bronchial cuff to ventilate right upper lobe
Reserved strictly for left pneumonectomy or left bronchial disruption
